overview: C0D is the one serverbound packet in this batch, and it is a state signal: closing a window flips the server-side inventory-open state, which is what inventory-move and chest-stealer detection keys on. Real consumers are Azure InvTweaksA (close while sprinting), Daedalus ActionProcessor (close clears openInventory), Intave InventoryTracker (close state plus the beacon special case) and Kauri's PacketHandler (both directions). The rest is wrappers (Artemis GPacketPlayClientWindowClose, FlopAC WrappedInCloseWindowPacket, BendEye-Perus isCloseWindow) and one keyword hit that never reads the packet: FlopAC InventoryC is a click-delay chest-stealer check driven by WINDOW_CLICK events.

checks.name: InvTweaksA (Azure)
checks.purpose: Classic inventory-tweaks detection: closing a window while sprinting is the walking-with-inventory-open tell.
checks.how_it_works: InvTweaksA hooks the inbound packet stream and checks the type: when PacketPlayInCloseWindow arrives while the Bukkit player is sprinting, it calls onViolation with a 60000 ms cooldown. Azure's PlayerStats also records the close-window type in its per-packet stats.
checks.detects: Inventory-tweaks and chest-stealer clients that close the GUI and keep sprinting, plus the walk-while-inventory-open pattern generally.
checks.variations: Azure is the only classic anticheat with a dedicated close-window check. Its PlayerStats counter (line 68) records the type in the same hook. No other classic anticheat in the corpus flags the close packet directly.

checks.name: ActionProcessor close-window state (Daedalus)
checks.purpose: State sync: a close-window packet clears the openInventory flag that Daedalus's inventory and movement checks read.
checks.how_it_works: ActionProcessor is fed by PacketListeners, which wraps the inbound close-window packet (line 103) and calls the update overload. The close-window overload sets openInventory = false, paired with the C0B OPEN_INVENTORY branch of the entity-action overload that sets it true. Checks that must know whether the player has a GUI open read the flag.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: state bookkeeping. It makes GUI-state-dependent checks such as inventory move and click timing accurate.
checks.variations: Kauri PacketHandler wraps both directions: the inbound CLOSE_WINDOW branch sets inventoryOpen false immediately (lines 271-273), and the server CLOSE_WINDOW branch defers the same write to a keepalive action (lines 538-540) so the state lands at the client's tick.

checks.name: InventoryTracker close-window state (Intave)
checks.purpose: Track the player's inventory-open state from the close-window packet, with a workaround for the beacon window that never sends one.
checks.how_it_works: InventoryTracker subscribes to the CLOSE_WINDOW inbound packet at LOW priority and closes the inventory: receiveCloseWindow calls closeInventory, which flips InventoryMetadata's open state to false. On the open side it special-cases the beacon container: since the client never sends a close packet for a beacon window, opening one skips the open-state update entirely, so the tracking never gets stuck with a stale open inventory.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: state tracking. The open and close state feeds the inventory-analysis checks, including the ChestStealer violations that the /intave history command reports.
checks.variations: FlopAC's InventoryC flags chest-stealer behavior from click-delay statistics but never reads the close-window packet; its C0D corpus hit is the flag message text only. Artemis's GPacketPlayClientWindowClose and FlopAC's WrappedInCloseWindowPacket are wrappers, and BendEye-Perus exposes isCloseWindow as a generic packet predicate.
